Why the Michael Jackson Movie Doesn’t Cover Sexual Abuse Allegations CN CitrixNews Staff · 

 In 2024, the creative team behind the Michael Jackson biopic got the kind of news that all Hollywood productions dread: Extensive reshoots were required. The film, announced in 2022 and delayed by the 2023 strikes, had finally begun production in January 2024 and principal photography had wrapped a few months later. Reshoots aren’t necessarily uncommon, but rather than needing to add or reconfigure a few scenes,  Michael  needed a drastic overhaul. The story wasn’t working. Not because of a convoluted plot or half-baked characters.

  In 1993, Jordan Chandler accused the King of Pop of molesting him. The allegations prompted a Los Angeles Police Department investigation, and Chandler’s family sued. Jackson eventually settled with the Chandlers in 1994 for about $20 million, after which the family stopped cooperating with the police and the case was closed with no charges. (Jackson repeatedly denied Chandler’s allegations, as well as all future accusations of sexual abuse .) 

  In January 2025,  Puck  reported for the first time that the delay was tied to the Chandler storyline. It indicated that the clause in the Chandler settlement was discovered after a September 2024  Financial Times  story that reported, for the first time, on new settlement payments the Jackson estate made to a different set of accusers in 2020. (These appear to be related to allegations made by the Cascio siblings, whose allegations against Jackson became public earlier this year. The Jackson estate has denied the accusations.) 

  Chanlder, of course, was not the only boy to come forward with allegations against Jackson. In 2003, Jackson was arrested and eventually charged on allegations that he abused 13-year-old Gavin Arvizo. The case went to trial in 2005, lasted three months, and eventually ended with Jackson’s acquittal on all charges.

While one claimed abuse over seven years, the other was allegedly abused over four years, starting when they were 10 years old. Both the accusers had, however, denied Jackson molested them back in 1993 when the allegations first surfaced against the popstar.

 In a 10-page civil claim filed Friday in the Los Angeles Superior Court, William Rosenthal, an assistant manager at the bar Good Times at Davey Wayne’s, is said to have denied entry to Fuqua, his son, Brando, and his daughter because they were “visibly overly intoxicated.” Rosenthal was then spat on by a member of the group, to which Rosenthal told them they needed to leave the bar.

 Rosenthal is seeking $50,000 as a result of his suffering “serious physical and psychological injuries” which include a nose fracture, head injury, skin lacerations, post-traumatic stress disorder, severe emotional distress and severe scarring, all of which continue to cause him “great physical and mental pain and suffering.” The claim noted that Rosenthal believes said injuries “will result in some permanent disability.” 

 Reps for Fuqua told Variety that “none of this is true.”
